decision: How should the report, the report email and Parent home show where the child's math can go with Unica, book by book, up to a goal grade?
evidence: Savar, 2026-11-11: after the first report, show a visual, easy plan tied to the curriculum (Book 1, Book 2, ...). Goal: below grade -> school grade; at grade -> school grade + 2; ahead -> working level + 2.
primary_axis: representation form (book path, grade chart, month list, milestone stops)
invariants: same child (Leah, Grade 3) in three cases: working at Grade 1, 3 and 4

same computed pace from the real BC curriculum (src/lib/workbook-curriculum): 10 days a book, the level's planned books, the last one the level test book; Book 1 at the first level of the working grade
same headline: 'At {d} days a week, {child} can reach a {Grade N} level by about {month year}.' and the same basis line
pace switch 3, 4 or 5 days a week moves every date
no level ids (U4) shown to a parent; grades label groups of books, never one level (D-218)
placed after the report's results and before the plan button; warm look tokens
assumptions_to_decide: Book 1 starts 5 weeks after the report (making plus the 14 to 35 day mail window in parent-view.ts); Parent home would count from the real delivery date
the goal is reached when the child starts the goal grade's first level (the same meaning as the report's working level)

options.bet: Show the books themselves: one tile per book, grouped by grade, from Today to a goal flag; topic cards under it
options.benefit: Ties the plan to what the family gets in the mail; Parent home can fill each tile as books are marked, on the same picture
options.cost: 20 to 24 tiles; on a phone the track must wrap (the mockup scrolls sideways)
options.risk: Many tiles can read as 'a lot of work' instead of 'a clear path'

options.bet: A chart: grade going up over months, with the school grade line and the goal flag
options.benefit: Reads like a projection at a glance; the pace switch visibly moves the goal; the best still image for the email
options.cost: Less about books and topics; chart labels are small on a phone
options.risk: A straight rising line looks like a promise of steady progress; parents may read it as a guarantee

options.bet: A month-by-month plan: which books and topics each month, with grade milestones and the goal
options.benefit: The most concrete: a parent sees what December holds; easy to mark real progress later
options.cost: The longest; needs 'Show all months'; weakest as one picture
options.risk: Feels like a schedule the child can fall behind on

options.bet: Three stops only: Book 1 now, the next grade, the goal, each with its date and main topics
options.benefit: The easiest to read in 5 seconds; the same on phone, email and Parent home
options.cost: Books are a count, not a picture; less 'program' feel
options.risk: Too plain to feel like a personal plan

recommendation: A, with each grade's tiles wrapping into rows on a phone, and its static render as the email image
